title: Predictive molecular dynamics from biological sequence

concept.text: Conceptual synthesis: This innovation would predict how biomolecules move, occupy different states, interact and change state, starting from biological sequence together with specified molecular partners and physical conditions. Its outputs would include molecular ensembles—the collection of accessible configurations—their populations, transition rates and interaction energetics. The target is an accurate, computationally practical method that also works for unfamiliar molecules and partners.

Conceptual synthesis: A predicted structure provides a configuration; the broader capability would explain how frequently different configurations occur, how quickly molecules move between them and how interactions change those behaviors. Sequence alone does not fully specify that prediction target: partners and conditions must also be defined. The concept therefore extends structural prediction toward quantitative, condition-dependent molecular behavior.

significance.text: Conditional impact synthesis: If sufficiently accurate and practical, this capability would make molecular mechanisms quantitatively testable at scale. Predicting state populations would address which functional configurations are available and how prevalent they are; predicting transition rates would address when those configurations become available and how long changes take. Predicting interaction energetics would connect molecular association and perturbations to changes in those populations.

Conditional downstream synthesis: Drug discovery could benefit from predictions of binding energetics, rare functional states and ligand-induced shifts. Enzyme engineering could benefit from predictions connecting sequence changes to molecular motion and functional states. These are plausible applications rather than demonstrated outcomes of the proposed innovation. Successful designs, biological effects and clinical outcomes would still require experiments.

Scope synthesis: The revolutionary step would be reliable prediction across molecules and contexts, rather than producing additional plausible configurations alone. Molecular prediction would not by itself establish cellular or organism-level behavior, where regulation, concentrations and interacting processes also matter. Achieving routine proteome-scale computation would be a separate substantial advance alongside predictive accuracy and generalization.

missing_breakthrough.text: Capability-gap synthesis: The missing capability is a method that jointly predicts ensembles, populations, transition rates and interaction energetics with useful accuracy, calibrated uncertainty and practical computational cost across specified conditions. The supplied evidence does not establish how broadly existing methods fall short of this target, so this is the innovation's proposed capability gap rather than a verified survey of all present approaches.

Scientific-barrier synthesis: The method must distinguish finding an accessible molecular configuration from estimating its population or the rate of reaching it. Rare functional states must be identified and assigned appropriate probabilities, while transitions between states require information about the processes connecting them. Predicting interaction energetics must also account for how association and changes in partners alter the ensemble. Accurate structural coordinates alone do not establish these quantities.

Engineering-barrier synthesis: Generalization must extend beyond familiar protein families and partners to unfamiliar molecules and combinations. Conditions and partner identities must be represented explicitly enough to define comparable prediction targets. The method must provide uncertainty estimates that reveal unreliable predictions, and its computational demands must remain low enough for the intended scale. Satisfying one requirement, such as generating diverse configurations cheaply, would not establish the remaining capabilities.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies Abramson et al.'s “Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3,” dated May 8, 2024, as a reported advance in predicting structures of complexes containing proteins, nucleic acids and small molecules. That description and date are carried as reported bibliographic and research information: the retained source available to the review contains only a cookie-access challenge, without article-specific scientific text sufficient to independently verify the article identity, demonstrated scope or limitations.

The retained PubMed material therefore cannot establish whether AlphaFold 3 demonstrated solution ensembles, state populations or transition kinetics, nor can it verify the limitations passage carried in the earlier research. The defensible conclusion from this supplied record is that the cited structural advance does not provide inspectable evidence here for the full proposed dynamics capability. This evidence limitation does not show that the reported 2024 result is false.

Evidence-boundary synthesis: The supplied bounded search record is empty, leaving coverage of developments through November 1, 2026 unresolved. The source-index retrieval dated November 11, 2026 records an access-limited artifact rather than a scientific update. No validated quantitative performance, computational-cost measurements or broader demonstration of the complete capability can be reported from these inputs.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Conduct blinded evaluations across unrelated protein families, complexes and explicitly specified physical conditions. Predict experimentally measured state populations, transition rates and interaction energetics, including binding free energies and their changes. Include rare functional states, ligand-induced ensemble shifts, and unfamiliar molecules and partners so that the evaluation covers the full concept rather than structural prediction or binding prediction alone.
completion_criteria.label: Blinded predictions capture populations, rates and energetics across unfamiliar molecules

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evaluation design: Define numerical accuracy, uncertainty-calibration and computational-cost thresholds before revealing test outcomes. Evaluate populations, rates and energetics separately so that strong performance on one cannot conceal failure on another. Document experimental uncertainty and the correspondence between experimental and predicted conditions. The supplied material does not justify particular numerical thresholds; these would need to be selected for the intended scientific uses.
completion_criteria.label: Predefined accuracy, calibration and cost thresholds assess each output separately

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: Make the evaluation inputs, prediction procedures and outcome comparisons available for independent replication, and confirm performance on additional held-out families, partners and conditions. Measure computational costs at a workload representative of routine proteome-scale use. Report the molecular classes and conditions actually tested, alongside failures and uncertain predictions. Finite tests would establish demonstrated breadth, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible evaluations report demonstrated breadth, proteome-scale costs and limitations

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BIF-09, “Proteome-scale prediction of molecular interactions and affinities,” isolates the valuable narrower goal of predicting which molecules bind and with what affinity. BIF-02 overlaps through interaction energetics and binding changes, but additionally requires ensembles, state populations and transition rates. Accurate affinity prediction would satisfy part of BIF-02's target without completing it; both remain distinct innovations.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-03, “A transferable, predictive virtual cell,” and BIF-04, “General reconstruction of causal cellular networks,” address broader cellular behavior and causal organization. Molecular dynamics predictions could supply mechanistic inputs to those efforts, but would not independently reconstruct cellular networks or establish a transferable cell model. BIF-01, “A predictive decoder for the regulatory genome,” and BIF-08, “Reliable reconstruction and forecasting of single-cell fates,” likewise target regulatory and cellular outcomes beyond the molecular ensembles considered here.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-06, “A general decoder for unknown gene and protein functions,” could benefit from predicted functional states and interactions, while still requiring interpretation connecting molecular behavior to biological roles. BIF-05, “Computer-aided design of functional whole genomes,” and BIF-13, “Predictive design of functional genetic circuits and pathways,” concern design at larger organizational scales. BIF-02 could inform component behavior in those designs without establishing the function of an entire genome, circuit or pathway.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-07, “Computational reconstruction of organism-scale molecular maps,” concerns molecular organization at organism scale. BIF-11, “Accessible, uncertainty-aware assembly of complex genomes,” and BIF-12, “Strain-resolved discovery and functional profiling of microbial communities,” concern reconstruction and profiling tasks that could supply biological inputs or contexts. BIF-10, “A broadly capable autonomous bioinformatics discovery system,” concerns coordinating discovery more broadly. These concepts may use or complement molecular predictions, but their stated goals remain separate from predicting molecular motion, populations, rates and energetics.

unresolved_issues: The retained source does not verify the AlphaFold 3 article identity, May 8, 2024 date, reported molecular scope or limitations concerning ensembles and kinetics.
The earlier limitations passage and reported history of multiple retrieval attempts remain unverified because supporting records were not supplied.
The breadth of existing capabilities and remaining gaps through November 1, 2026 cannot be established from the empty bounded search record.
Numerical success thresholds for populations, rates, interaction energetics, uncertainty calibration and computational cost remain unspecified.
The intended molecular classes, range of physical conditions, definition of unfamiliar partners and workload for routine proteome-scale use require operational definitions.

brief.title: Predicting how life's molecules move and interact
possible: Drug researchers could predict which shapes a biological molecule takes, how often each occurs, how quickly it changes shape and how strongly it binds other molecules. They would start from its sequence—the order of its building blocks—and specify its partners and physical conditions.
why: These predictions would help researchers test explanations of how molecules work. Drug developers could target rarely occupied shapes and anticipate how binding changes molecular behavior. Enzyme designers could connect sequence changes to motion and function.

sources.who: Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs and collaborators
sources.showed: AlphaFold 3 predicted the structures of complexes containing proteins, genetic material and small molecules, outperforming specialized methods in most categories tested.
sources.quote: In all but one category, it achieves a substantially higher performance than strong methods that specialize in just the given task
sources.cited_for: Predicting structures of interacting molecules is an established step toward predicting their behavior.
sources.not_established: Accurate structures alone do not establish how often different shapes occur or how quickly molecules move between them.

sources.who: Sarah Lewis, Tim Hempel and colleagues
sources.showed: BioEmu generated collections of protein shapes and estimated their relative likelihoods and folding stability. It captured motions that expose hidden binding sites.
sources.quote:
It captures diverse
functional motions—including cryptic pocket formation, local
unfolding, and domain rearrangements
sources.cited_for: Fast prediction can extend beyond individual structures to collections of shapes and their probabilities.
sources.not_established: The work does not establish transition speeds or the full behavior of molecules interacting with different partners.

sources.who: Gabriel Monteiro da Silva and colleagues
sources.showed: A modified AlphaFold method predicted changes in how often proteins occupy different shapes. Tests covered a small protein sample and worked best for qualitative changes in common shapes.
sources.quote: predicted changes in their relative state populations with more than 80% accuracy.
sources.cited_for: Sequence information can help predict shifts in the relative likelihoods of protein shapes.
sources.not_established: The small study does not establish broadly accurate probabilities, transition speeds or binding strengths.

sources.who: Conor D. Parks and colleagues at the Drug Design Data Resource
sources.showed: A blinded competition tested predictions of how small molecules bind proteins and how strongly they bind. Some methods successfully ranked binding strengths.
sources.quote: All the ligands bind the same region of the protein
sources.cited_for: Blinded comparisons can test binding predictions against experiments without revealing answers beforehand.
sources.not_established: Binding rankings for selected targets do not establish complete molecular behavior from sequence.

sources.who: Gregory A. Ross and colleagues at Schrödinger
sources.showed: Physics-based binding calculations could approach experimental reproducibility with carefully prepared structures. Experimental measurements themselves varied in accuracy.
sources.quote:
We ﬁnd a wide variability in experimental
accuracy and a correspondence between binding and functional assays.
sources.cited_for: Binding predictions need comparisons that account for uncertainty in experimental measurements.
sources.not_established: These calculations require molecular structures and do not establish the full prediction capability from sequence.

shown: Researchers have demonstrated separate parts of the capability. Google DeepMind and collaborators predicted structures of interacting molecules. Lewis and colleagues used BioEmu to generate collections of protein shapes and estimate their probabilities and stability.

Monteiro da Silva and colleagues predicted changes in shape probabilities in a small study. Binding studies have also predicted differences in binding strength. These results have not established a practical method that combines all the required predictions across unfamiliar molecules.
missing: A single method must accurately predict shapes, their probabilities, transition speeds and binding energies together.
Predictions must cover rare functional shapes and changes caused by different partners and physical conditions.
Reliable performance must extend to unfamiliar molecules, with uncertainty estimates that identify unreliable predictions.
Computational costs must be practical for routine use across an organism's full set of proteins.

milestones.label: Blinded predictions match behavior across unfamiliar molecules
milestones.explanation: Tests with hidden answers would have to match measured shape probabilities, transition speeds and binding energies across unrelated molecules and specified conditions. This would test the full capability.

milestones.label: Each output meets predefined accuracy, uncertainty and cost thresholds
milestones.explanation: Each output would have to meet thresholds set before results are revealed, accounting for experimental uncertainty and matching conditions. This would prevent success on one output from hiding failure on another.

milestones.label: Independent tests confirm breadth and practical computing costs
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce results on further unfamiliar cases and measure costs for workloads spanning an organism's proteins. This would establish practical reach, including failures and uncertain predictions.

uncertain: What accuracy and uncertainty thresholds would make each prediction useful for its intended scientific purpose?
Which molecular classes, conditions and unfamiliar partners should the tests cover?
What workload and computing cost would qualify as routine use across an organism's full set of proteins?

page.title: Sequence-based prediction of protein ensembles and kinetics
page.definition: A method predicts a protein’s accessible structures, their equilibrium populations, transition rates and partner-binding free energies from its amino-acid sequence, specified partners and solution conditions. An ensemble is a collection of structures weighted by their probabilities.

goal.need: A survey of experimental reproducibility and a separate calculation benchmark show a remaining gap in binding energetics. Predicting molecular motion also requires populations and rates: equilibrium sampling alone supplies no transition times. The goal combines these quantities under specified partners and solution conditions.

figures.caption: Agreement of relative binding free energies reported on 14 October 2023.
figures.note: The calculation benchmark and experimental survey contain different molecular series; these percentages are not a paired comparison.

statements.context: Topics identified under “Future work” in the AlphaFold proteome-scale announcement.

completion.title: Independent replication confirms blinded prediction of protein ensembles, kinetics and binding free energies.
completion.criterion: One fixed method, given protein sequences, partner identities and solution conditions, passes a blinded evaluation on families and partners excluded from training and tuning; an independent team replicates the pass on another held-out panel. Every discrete reference conformation has global TM-score >0.75. Population-sensitive observables, state populations, transition rate constants and absolute binding free energies agree with independent measurements within their reported experimental uncertainties. Temperature, pH, ionic composition and partners match the experiments.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; a combined test synthesized from the cited goals and component assessments.
completion.basis: Searches of CASP ensemble assessments, D3R/SAMPL challenges, molecular-dynamics validation guidance and BioEmu developer documents found no joint test covering populations, kinetics, affinity and generalization from sequence. This test combines the cited goals. Agreement within experimental uncertainty and independent replication are Atlas requirements, not a published field-wide acceptance standard.

milestones.title: Protein models recover reference conformations with global TM-score above 0.75 in a blinded CASP test.
milestones.criterion: Recover the reference states assessed for a multistate protein target with global TM-score >0.75, a measure of overall structural similarity. CASP16 defined successful modeling using this threshold for folds and spatial arrangements. Its assessment, published on 28 October 2025, reported success for five of ten biomolecular ensemble targets. One successful target, T1214, already had a publicly available unbound-state structure. This criterion does not establish population weights or transition rates.
milestones.set_by: CASP16 conformational-ensemble assessors, Dube et al., Results; the published assessment includes proteins, nucleic acids and complexes.
milestones.threshold_quote: with global TM scores > 0.75, corresponding to backbone RMSDs of 1.5 to 2 Å

milestones.title: GMCSF ensembles predict larger mutation-induced conformational shifts at H15/H83 than at H87.
milestones.criterion: For granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GMCSF), sequence-derived ensembles predict larger changes in conformational distributions for mutations at histidines 15 and 83 than at histidine 87, matching nuclear magnetic resonance measurements. This is one published validation axis, rather than a test of absolute populations. The paper of 27 March 2024 reported this ordering; across GMCSF and Abl1 kinase it reported >80% accuracy for population-change predictions, with mutation-specific failures.
milestones.set_by: Monteiro da Silva et al., GMCSF experimental-validation protocol; this criterion was written for one protein.
milestones.threshold_quote: if they predicted mutations to H15 and H83 to provoke larger changes in the distribution of conformations than mutations to H87

milestones.title: A sequence-based model predicts protein populations and transition rates within experimental uncertainty.
milestones.criterion: For a defined protein system under matched solution conditions, predict equilibrium state populations and transition rate constants from sequence. Both agree with independent measurements within their stated uncertainties, without fitting the test measurements. Component evidence: BioEmu’s 14 August 2025 paper reported mean absolute folding-free-energy error <0.9 kcal/mol for mutants drawn from 95 wild types. A study published on 20 July 2012 simulated four villin variants; calculated absolute folding rates were approximately threefold slower than experiment. These results do not establish the joint threshold.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas; the searched ensemble and folding-validation studies supplied component comparisons but no common joint population-and-rate acceptance threshold.

milestones.title: Relative protein–ligand binding free energies have mean unsigned error at most 1 kcal/mol.
milestones.criterion: For a defined protein–ligand benchmark, the mean absolute difference between predicted and measured relative binding free energies is ≤1 kcal/mol. This is a field-used accuracy target, not a universal acceptance standard. On 14 October 2023, Ross et al. reported weighted pairwise mean unsigned error of 0.98 kcal/mol, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.91–1.05 kcal/mol. These calculations used structural inputs and establish an energetic component rather than prediction of the complete behavior from sequence.
milestones.set_by: Protein–ligand free-energy prediction convention described explicitly by Khalak et al.; the stated target concerns relative binding free energies.
milestones.threshold_quote: state-of-the-art accuracy threshold of 1 kcal mol−1 achievable for relative binding free energy calculations.

milestones.title: One method passes a blinded joint test of protein ensembles, rates and absolute binding free energies.
milestones.criterion: A frozen method predicts conformations, populations, transition rates and absolute binding free energies from sequences, partners and solution conditions for families and partners withheld from training and tuning. Discrete reference states have global TM-score >0.75; quantitative outputs agree with independent measurements within experimental uncertainties. One blinded evaluation passes before independent replication. Microsoft’s 2026 BioEmu-2 model card supports partner-conditioned structural ensembles but excludes calibrated ensemble probabilities and binding-affinity prediction; this is developer documentation, not peer-reviewed validation.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas; the integration stage preceding independent replication in the completion test.

not_found: No independently replicated blinded demonstration jointly covering ensembles, populations, transition rates and absolute binding free energies on held-out protein families and partners was located.
No defined threshold for routine proteome-scale runtime or monetary cost was found.
No shared uncertainty-calibration criterion spanning populations, rates and binding free energies was found.
